finalText:
Both save changes from one branch into another, but they leave different marks in history.

**Merge** adds a new commit that joins two branches together. Your old commits stay exactly as they were, and you get a branch line that shows two paths coming together. Nothing gets rewritten, so it's safe on shared branches.

**Rebase** takes your commits and replants them on top of another branch, one by one. History ends up as one straight line, no join commit. But it rewrites commit history — so if anyone else already pulled those commits, their copy and yours will disagree.

Rule of thumb: rebase your own branch to keep it clean before sharing it. Merge when joining work back into a shared branch like `main`, or once other people already have copies of the commits.
